title: Linear Algebra for Modeling & Robotics
description: Vectors, matrices, eigenstructure, least squares, and linear transformations applied to state estimation, circuit networks, and robot coordinates.

modifications: Expanded the week-1 linear-systems prototype with reversible elimination, a worked unique solution, rank and consistency criteria, free-variable cases, numerical limits, and further-study links.

Expanded the week-2 vector-space prototype with span and independence tests, basis matrices, forward and inverse coordinate conversion, active versus passive rotations, and numerical-conditioning limits.

Expanded the week-7 eigenvalue prototype across discrete- and continuous-time systems, with mode decomposition, stability criteria, transition-matrix interpretation, and limits of diagonalization and local linearization.
Expanded the week-4 least-squares prototype with the normal-equation derivation, a synthetic three-observation fit, residual orthogonality and diagnostics, conditioning and weighting limits.

Expanded the week-3 rank/null-space lesson to compute all four fundamental subspaces of a synthetic rectangular matrix, connect rank and nullity in both ambient spaces, test consistency by left-null orthogonality, and interpret a least-squares residual.

outcomes.description: Solve linear systems and diagnose singularity.
Interpret bases, rank, and null spaces.
Use eigenvalues to describe linear dynamics.
Fit an overdetermined model by least squares.

lesson_objectives.description: Solve Ax=b with elimination.
Interpret pivots and rank as information about solutions.
Test linear independence and span.
Distinguish a geometric vector from its coordinates in a basis.
Interpret eigenvalues in discrete- and continuous-time linear dynamics.
Connect diagonalization to mode-by-mode behavior.
Derive normal equations for a full-rank linear model.
Interpret residuals and avoid overclaiming from fit quality.
Write a straight-line fit as an overdetermined system Ax ≈ b and form and solve the normal equations AᵀAx = Aᵀb.
Compute residuals and R², and explain why the residual vector is orthogonal to the columns of A.
Use a fitted calibration to estimate an unknown and evaluate when the fit or its use is unreliable.
Write a transition matrix for a two-state Markov chain and propagate a population distribution forward in time.
Compute the stationary distribution as the eigenvector for eigenvalue 1 and interpret it.
Use the second eigenvalue to determine how fast the population approaches the stationary distribution and evaluate the model's assumptions.
Compute the rank and nullity of a matrix by elimination and relate them through the rank–nullity theorem.
Decide whether a system Ax = b is consistent and describe all of its solutions.
Identify unknowns that cannot be identified, and compute the minimum-norm solution.
Compute the orthogonal projection of a vector onto another and verify that the residual is orthogonal to it.
Build an orthonormal basis for two vectors by Gram–Schmidt and write the QR factorization.
Solve a least-squares problem by back-substitution with R and compute the residual norm.
Compute the eigenvalues and orthonormal eigenvectors of a 2 × 2 symmetric matrix and check the trace and determinant.
Evaluate a quadratic form and determine from the eigenvalues whether a symmetric matrix is positive definite.
Interpret the largest eigenvalue and its eigenvector as the direction of greatest variance of a covariance matrix.
Compute the singular values of a small matrix from the eigenvalues of AᵀA.
Compute the energy captured by a rank-k approximation and the error of the approximation.
Count the storage saved by a low-rank approximation and evaluate when it is useful.
Apply condition numbers and fixed-matrix perturbation bounds.
Distinguish residual size, conditioning and numerical stability.
Calculate and interpret a scaled ridge estimate.
Compute centered sample covariance and its principal axes.
Calculate PCA scores, variance fractions and reconstruction errors.
Evaluate scaling, confounding and held-out preprocessing.
Diagnose directional sensitivity despite a small residual.
Propagate noise covariance and distinguish precision from bias.
Specify geometry redesign and independent reference validation.
Solve repeated synthetic sensor pairs and summarize parameter errors.
Compare directional sensitivity and independent-noise uncertainty.
Evaluate residuals, calibration bias and validation design.
Compute bases and dimensions for the row, column, null and left-null spaces, and use their orthogonality to analyze consistency and least-squares residuals.
Interpret det A as the signed area or volume scale factor of x ↦ Ax and use det A ≠ 0 as a test for invertibility linked to pivots, rank and the null space.
Compute a determinant by elimination and by cofactor expansion, and apply the rules for row operations, products, transposes, inverses and scalar multiples.
Connect the determinant to eigenvalues through det(A − λI) = 0 and explain why a determinant's size does not measure closeness to singularity.

duration.equivalent_structure: Proposed 14-week scope only, with unmeasured workload and no human review. All four compact legacy prototype units now have expanded readings alongside the other original lessons and synthetic-data lab. All activities are formative; this is not evidence of semester equivalence. Week 3 now connects the column and row spaces with the null and left-null spaces for a rectangular matrix, including consistency and least-squares residual geometry.

lessons.title: Linear systems, elimination, and rank
lessons.worked_example: For x+y=3 and x-y=1, elimination gives y=1 and x=2, with two pivots for two variables and one solution. Repeating the first equation gives rank 1 and infinitely many solutions; changing its right-hand side to 7 makes the system inconsistent.

modules.title: Vector spaces, bases, and coordinate transforms

lessons.title: Vector spaces, bases, and coordinate transforms
lessons.worked_example: With basis columns b1=(1,0) and b2=(1,1), coordinates (3,1) represent the standard vector (4,1). Multiplying by the basis matrix converts to standard coordinates; its inverse recovers basis coordinates. A 90-degree active rotation of (3,0) gives (0,3), while expressing the unchanged vector in the rotated frame gives (0,-3).

lessons.title: Eigenvalues and linear dynamical systems
lessons.worked_example: For a discrete diagonal system with eigenvalues 0.8 and -0.5 and initial state (1,2), three steps give components (0.512,-0.25): one decays steadily and the other alternates while shrinking. In continuous time, a mode with eigenvalue -2 decays as e^(-2t), with e-folding time 0.5.

lessons.title: Least squares and data fitting
lessons.worked_example: For synthetic data (0,1), (1,2), and (2,2), the normal equations yield intercept 7/6 and slope 1/2. The residuals are (-1/6, 1/3, -1/6), orthogonal to both the intercept and predictor columns, with residual sum of squares 1/6; this fit does not validate the model.

lessons.title: Least squares as linear algebra: fitting a calibration line, normal equations and reading residuals
lessons.worked_example: The normal equations for the synthetic standards give y = 0.100 + 1.970x with R² = 0.9984; the residuals sum to zero because they are orthogonal to the column of ones; a signal of 5.0 reads back as 2.487 μM.

lessons.title: Cell-state transitions as a Markov chain: transition matrices, the eigenvalue 1 and how fast a population settles
lessons.worked_example: With switching probabilities 0.2 (A to B) and 0.1 (B to A) per day, two days take an all-A population to 0.660 in A; the stationary fraction in A is 0.333; the second eigenvalue 0.7 halves deviations every 1.94 days.

modules.title: Rank, four fundamental subspaces and identifiability

lessons.title: Rank, null space and all four fundamental subspaces: counting independent information
lessons.worked_example: For A = [[1, 2, 1], [2, 4, 2], [3, 6, 3]] the rank is 1 and the nullity 2, b = (2, 4, 6) is in the column space (x = (2, 0, 0)) and the solutions form a plane; in the lesson, the mixing matrix of rank 2 has the null vector (1, 1, −1), no solution for b = (6, 11, 4), and a minimum-norm solution of length 1.6330 for b = (6, 12, 4). In B = [[1,1,0,0],[0,1,1,0],[1,2,1,0]], rank is 2; bases for C(B), N(B), C(Bᵀ) and N(Bᵀ) have dimensions 2, 2, 2 and 1. The left-null vector (−1,−1,1) shows that b=(2,1,4) is inconsistent; its least-squares residual is (−1/3,−1/3,1/3).

lessons.title: Orthogonality, projections and QR: the geometry behind least squares
lessons.worked_example: Projecting b = (1, 4, 1) onto a = (2, 1, 2) gives the coefficient 0.8889 and a residual of length 3.2998, and the QR solution of A = [[3, 1], [0, 2]] with b = (6, 4) is x = (1.3333, 2); in the lesson, the line fitted to (1, 1), (2, 2), (3, 2) is y = 0.6667 + 0.5x with residual norm 0.4082.

lessons.title: Symmetric matrices, the spectral theorem and quadratic forms
lessons.worked_example: For C = [[5, 2], [2, 2]] the eigenvalues are 6.0000 and 1.0000, the dominant eigenvector is at 26.57° and carries 0.857 of the total variance; in the lesson, A = [[4, 1], [1, 3]] has eigenvalues 4.6180 and 2.3820, a dominant direction at 31.72° and a variance of 4.5 along (1, 1)/√2.

lessons.title: The singular value decomposition and low-rank approximation
lessons.worked_example: For A = [[1, 1], [1, −1], [2, 0]] the singular values are 2.4495 and 1.4142, the first carries 0.75 of the energy and the rank-one error is 1.4142; in the lesson, A = [[3, 1], [2, 2], [1, 3]] has singular values 4.8990 and 2.0, a rank-one error of 2.0 and a relative error of 0.378.

lessons.title: Conditioning, error bounds and regularization
lessons.worked_example: For the synthetic matrix A = [[1, 0.99], [0.99, 1]], the singular gains are 1.99 and 0.01 and the condition number is 199. An opposite signal perturbation of (0.01, −0.01) changes the estimate by (1, −1). Ridge introduces a stated preference; the better geometry has condition number 1.5.

lessons.title: Centered PCA, scaling and interpretation
lessons.worked_example: Centering four synthetic observations gives covariance [[8/3, 4/3], [4/3, 4/3]], with eigenvalues 3.490712 and 0.509288. The first component explains 0.872678 of variance, and the rank-one reconstruction error is 1.236068. Standardization changes the variance fraction and axes; confounded separation does not establish mechanism.

modules.title: Two displacement sensors: a small residual and an unreliable answer

lessons.title: Two displacement sensors: a small residual and an unreliable answer
lessons.worked_example: A poor sensor geometry fits the noisy signal pair exactly yet swaps reference displacement (2, 3) to (3, 2). With independent equal signal noise of standard deviation 0.01, coordinate standard deviation is 0.707116 for poor geometry and 0.010623 for improved geometry. Fixed calibration bias does not average away.

lessons.title: Determinants: volume scaling, row operations and invertibility
lessons.worked_example: For C = [[1, 2, 0], [3, 4, 1], [0, 2, 5]], elimination gives pivots 1, −2 and 6, so det C = −12, confirmed by cofactor expansion along row 1; C is invertible, det(2C) = −96 and det(C⁻¹) ≈ −0.0833. In the lesson, A = [[2, 1, 3], [4, 5, 7], [−2, 4, 1]] has pivots 2, 3 and 7/3 (det 14), B needs one row exchange (det −6), and S = [[1, 2, 3], [2, 4, 7], [3, 6, 10]] is singular with null-space vector (−2, 1, 0).

modules.title: Virtual lab 1: sensor geometry, noise and displacement estimates

lessons.title: Virtual lab 1: sensor geometry, noise and displacement estimates
lessons.worked_example: Ten synthetic paired-error signal observations are solved row by row. Both geometries give mean displacement (2, 3) because the errors deliberately balance, while parameter RMSE is 2 for poor geometry and 0.025 for improved geometry. Zero residual and an accurate mean do not establish real calibration accuracy.

grading_policy.attempt_policy: Unlimited formative retries; no summative grade is awarded.
grading_policy.solution_release: Public practice solutions may be shown after an attempt. They are not production exam keys.
grading_policy.late_policy: No deadlines or late penalties exist in this partial package.

history.summary: Preserved original compact prototype content in separate manifests and readings; labeled partial without semester or credit equivalency.

Added two original lessons (least-squares calibration with normal equations and residuals; Markov chains for cell-state transitions with stationary distributions and convergence rates) with synthetic data, formative items with computed keys and retrieval cards. The package remains partial and unreviewed.

Assessments with items now also list the course outcomes those items assess, derived from each item's lesson objective and that objective's outcome links. The rubric-only case lists none, and neither do the 4 prototype-unit assessments, whose objectives are not yet linked to an outcome. No readings, items or keys changed. The syllabus was regenerated from the manifest: it states the current version, lists every lesson with its item and card counts, and describes the current practice and limitations (it still described only the four original units). The course limitations shown to learners were also updated: they still described one formative check per lesson and the original numerical rules. The package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added seven original lessons on rank and identifiability, projection and QR, symmetric spectra, SVD, conditioning and ridge, centered PCA, and a two-sensor displacement case; one synthetic sensor-geometry lab; and a proposed 14-week schedule. Recovered Claude drafts were corrected and extended with Codex assistance. No new sources. Still partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the week-1 linear-systems reading with worked elimination, rank and consistency reasoning, free-variable cases, and numerical interpretation limits. Linked both lesson objectives and its practice assessment to course outcomes 1 and 2. Existing questions, answer keys and cards are unchanged; three compact legacy units remain. The course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the week-2 vector-space reading with basis and coordinate conversions, span and independence, and active versus passive rotation examples. Linked both objectives and the practice assessment to outcome 2. Existing questions, answer keys and cards are unchanged; two compact legacy readings remain. The course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the week-7 eigenvalue reading across discrete and continuous dynamics, including modal behavior, stability, transition matrices, diagonalization limits, and local linearization. Corrected objective 1 to match the existing continuous-time question and mapped both objectives and the practice assessment to outcome 3. Existing questions, answer keys and cards are unchanged; one compact legacy reading remains. The course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the week-4 least-squares reading with the normal-equation derivation, a synthetic overdetermined fit, residual orthogonality and diagnostics, and numerical conditioning limits. Linked both objectives and the practice assessment to outcome 4. Existing question prompts, answers and cards are unchanged. All four compact legacy prototypes now have expanded instruction; the course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added a public synthetic hidden-state reconstruction and transition-dynamics project draft, with an exact five-channel least-squares dataset, QR/rank/conditioning checks, an orthonormal contrast basis, eigenmode propagation, and an unweighted review rubric. The project is inactive and ungraded; the course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the existing rank/null-space unit with an original 3×4 matrix example that computes bases and dimensions for all four fundamental subspaces, checks the rank/nullity identities and orthogonal pairs, tests right-hand-side consistency, and interprets a least-squares residual in the left null space. Added six formative problems and four retrieval cards while retaining the 14-week proposal. The course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added an original determinants reading grouped with eigenvalues in week 7, following the MIT OCW 18.06SC Fall 2011 Unit II order: determinants as signed area/volume scale factors, the three row-operation rules, elimination with pivot products and exchange signs, cofactor expansion and its cost, product/inverse/transpose/scalar rules, the invertibility equivalences, Cramer's rule in context, det(A − λI) = 0, and why a determinant's size does not measure conditioning. Three objectives, eleven formative items and four cards; the eigenvalue lesson links to it. The syllabus no longer describes the expanded week-1/2/4/7 readings as short prototypes. No week was added. The course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

limitations: All four compact legacy prototype units now have expanded instruction alongside the other original lessons and synthetic-data virtual lab; this package is not equivalent to a full university semester.

A proposed 14-week schedule exists but is unmeasured and unreviewed. There is one synthetic-data lab, no substantive homework sequence or laboratory sequence, and no midterm or final. An inactive integrative project draft is not scheduled or graded.
Public formative items and objective associations remain provisional and do not demonstrate comprehensive coverage or mastery.
Bloom labels and prerequisite edges are authoring classifications awaiting subject-matter review.
Answers and solution feedback are intentionally public practice authoring specifications, not restricted exam keys.
Of the 69 numeric item answers, 2 require a unit; none checks significant figures or dimensions. CSV checks use explicit tolerances and optional units.
Total workload and weekly duration are unknown; a proposed sequence is not workload evidence.

All new matrices, displacements and observations are synthetic. Sensor comparisons assume stated calibration scales and noise; no real tissue experiment, clinical interpretation or device specification is established.
intentionally_omitted: Graded assessments, a laboratory sequence, an activated cumulative project, measured workload and qualified human review remain unauthored.
